questions.prompt: Which cache dedupes identical fetch calls within a single render pass?
questions.explanation: Request Memoization (a React feature) dedupes identical fetch calls during one render; it lasts only for that render.

questions.prompt: Which server cache stores persistent fetch results across requests? Type its two-word name.
questions.explanation: The Data Cache holds fetch results on the server across requests and deployments; you control it with cache/revalidate.

questions.prompt: Which statements are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: The Full Route Cache stores statically rendered route output
The Router Cache lives in the browser for the session
In Next.js 15, fetch fills the Data Cache automatically

questions.explanation: The Full Route Cache holds static output, the Router Cache is client-side, and revalidate* clears server caches. In Next.js 15 you must opt into caching fetch.

questions.prompt: Match each cache to its scope.
questions.explanation: Memoization is per-render, the Data Cache persists across requests, the Full Route Cache holds static output, and the Router Cache is client-side.

questions.prompt: Order the caches from innermost (one render) to outermost (browser).
questions.explanation: Memoization (one render) → Data Cache (across requests) → Full Route Cache (rendered output) → Router Cache (client navigation).
